correctness.rationale: Independent re-execution from scratch confirms every essential claim. Order: brute-force enumeration of 13^4=28561 matrices gives |SL(2,13)|=2184 matching q(q^2-1)=13*168; center {+-I} size 2 (13 odd, -I!=I, det(-I)=1) so |PSL|=1092. Canonical representative canon(M)=min(M,-M) is well-defined (M!=-M for det=1) and coincides on all 2184 SL elements with alternative first-nonzero-in-1..6 convention (0 mismatches). Generators a=[[1,1],[0,1]], b=[[1,0],[1,1]], A=a^-1, B=b^-1 satisfy mm(a,A)=mm(b,B)=I; none equals +-I (L=1 zero hits); a^13=b^13=I and a^k=+-I iff 13|k verified to k<=26 (a^k=[[1,k],[0,1]] never -I). Regularity: BFS neighbors of identity are 4 distinct canonical classes; L=2 reduced enumeration (12 words, 0 hits) independently proves no generator squares to +-I and no two distinct generators coincide mod +-I, so Gamma is simple 4-regular; spot-checked at 5 vertices. Diameter: two independent BFS implementations (different canon functions and opposite neighbor orders a,A,b,B vs B,b,A,a) both cover 1092 vertices, give identical spheres [1,4,12,25,48,96,180,279,317,120,10] summing to 1092, max depth 10, ball<=9=1082. All 10 diametral canonical elements with length-10 words verified to evaluate correctly and lie at distance 10. w_D=aaaaabbbba evaluates raw to (8,0,4,5) whose canon is (5,0,9,8) at BFS distance 10; exhaustive reduced-word search to length 9 (39363 words, no hit to target) plus BFS distance proves no shorter word (any unreduced word has a reduced form no longer via adjacent-inverse cancellation, spot-checked on 1000 random words) so distance exactly 10 and diameter exactly 10. Girth: two independent enumerators (recursive DFS and explicit-stack DFS) plus auditor's independent iterative enumerator agree: L=1:4/0, 2:12/0, 3:36/0, 4:108/0, 5:324/0 (484 words total, 0 hits), 6:972/28 hits. Witness w_g=aaBaaB is reduced and stepwise multiplies to -I=[[12,0],[0,12]] (a^2=[[1,2],[0,1]] -> *B -> *a -> *a -> *B = -I), hence identity in PSL. All 28 length-6 hits sorted list matches results.json exactly; split +I=12/-I=16 verified, each reduced identity. Since L<=5 has 0 hits, shortest reduced identity has length 6; with L=1,2 zero hits excluding loops/multi-edges, graph girth equals shortest reduced identity length, so girth=6. Auxiliary claims verified: L=7:2916/0, L=8:8748/120, L=9:26244/0, L=10:78732/536. replay.py passes all 9 asserts in <1s. This is exhaustive computational proof over a finite set (deterministic BFS/DFS + pure 2x2 matmul mod 13), not sampled experimental evidence.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval on 2026-09-07 confirms no prior exact diameter/girth table for this stratum. Gap query arXiv all:PSL2 AND all:13 AND all:Cayley returns 0 hits. Broader queries return only asymptotic or structural work: Garonzi-Halasi-Somlai 2022 and Halasi 2020 prove polylog Babai-type diameter upper bounds for transvection-containing generating sets in PSL(n,q)/SL(n,p) with no exact p=13 census, no distance distribution, no diametral word, no girth witness; Chen 2016 classifies regular balanced Cayley maps (surface embeddings) on PSL(2,p) with no word metric or BFS computation; Helfgott 2008 proves growth/generation implying O((log p)^c) diameter for SL(2,p) with no small-prime exact tables. Crossref query PSL2 13 Cayley diameter exact returns only unrelated Hl,p exact-diameter and PSL2(p) Hamilton-cycle records. No source gives D=10, spheres [1,4,12,25,48,96,180,279,317,120,10], w_D=aaaaabbbba, g=6, w_g=aaBaaB or the 28 length-6 relations for the canonical elementary-transvection pair a=[[1,1],[0,1]], b=[[1,0],[1,1]]. The certificate pair (diametral word + shortest relation, both replayable by 2x2 matmul) is therefore substantively new, not a restatement or parameter tweak of an existing table.

value.rationale: Result is independently worth finding later as a citable benchmark stratum. Object is canonical: G=PSL(2,13) with the elementary transvection pair, the standard generators for SL(2,p), yielding a 4-regular graph on 1092 vertices small enough for seconds-long replay but large enough that exact diameter/girth are not in literature. Claim sits between textbook finiteness (Schreier-Sims/order formula) and deep asymptotics (Helfgott polylog, Babai conjecture) and is directly cited for diameter benchmarks and Cayley-hash cryptography parameters per topic motivation. It is not a textbook restatement (textbooks give q(q^2-1) but not D=10, spheres, or g=6), not mere parameter substitution (no prior table for other p with same method to substitute; canonical pair plus reusable certificate format, full distance distribution, 10 diametral words, 28 relations with +I/-I split, and L=7-10 auxiliary counts), not a tiny unmotivated gain (complete diameter+girth census with explicit witnesses, not an epsilon improvement), and not an unexplained enumeration (conventions fixed: undirected, reduced-word girth, PSL identity=+-I; counts explained and replayable in <1s stdlib-only). Single-stratum scope is honestly limited but the stratum itself closes one quotation-ready gap.
